DISCUSSION ITEMS a.
Review of the Governor’s FY2025 Recommended Budget Enclosure 2.a.
Vice Chair Sabitoni introduced Abby Benson, Interim Vice President for Administration and Finance who provided a presentation on the Governor’s FY2025 Recommended Budget.
This presentation can be found in Enclosure 2.a.
Her presentation included discussions of the University’s FY2025 Appropriation Request, with respect to the FY2024 request and enacted amounts; details regarding the University’s current service level; strategic initiatives; RICAP; and the pending General Obligation Bond (Biomedical Life Sciences Building). b.
Tuition and Fee Rates Review Enclosure 2.b.
Interim Vice President Benson provided a presentation on tuition and fees for FY 2025.
The presentation can be found in Enclosure 2.b.
She noted that the Board had approved permanently moving the approval of tuition and fees from the September meeting to the February meeting.

Interim Vice President Benson’s presentation covered the total cost of attendance (TCOA) (noting the assumptions used in this calculation) by discussing 1) Housing and Dining rates, noting a 3.6% increase in these areas collectively, 2) mandatory fees, noting a 0.9% fee increase overall, and 3) tuition.
Interim VP Benson introduced Dean Libutti, Associate Vice President for Enrollment Management and Student Success, who discussed enrollment planning for FY2025, noting zero changes to the FY2025 First-Year target (with a small shift between in-state and out-of-state students) and a forty-five-student decrease in transfers.
He also presented assumptions regarding enrollments across the University.
Interim Vice President Benson provided a recommendation to the Committee for a 3.5% increase in tuition across the board, noting that this amount provides maximum revenue while managing potential enrollment declines.
She discussed the assumptions used for building this model.
Dean Libutti noted that the assumptions used in this model are based on macroeconomic analyses, internal data, and anecdotal information from URI students and parents.

Interim Vice President Benson introduced John Poehlmann, Assistant Vice President for Financial Strategy and Planning, who discussed URI’s TCOA compared to URI’s regional peers.
In addition, he provided detail on modeling scenarios for undergraduate and graduate populations that provided for the recommended tuition increase.
In addition, John Poehlmann discussed strategies for expanding graduate enrollments.

The University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees Finance and Facilities Committee Charter Created 6/26/2020 Amended 10/24/2020 Amended 6/29/2023 Membership: At least three voting members of the Board are appointed annually by the Board Chair upon the recommendation of the Governance Committee and in consultation with the University President. The Board Chair will appoint a Chair and a Vice Chair for the committee. Purposes: A primary purpose of the committee is to oversee fulfillment of the Board’ s fiduciary responsibility through the provision of appropriate human, physical, financial, and technology resources. The committee is responsible for the provis ion of the necessary physical and technological infrastructure to support the mission and strategic vision of the University. The committee reviews and recommends for Board approval the university ’s budget including tuition and fees, the university ’s audit ed financial statements, major capital projects, and real estate transactions, and requests for borrowing. Specific duties include: • Monitor the University’s financial operations; • Review and recommend annual and long-range operating and capital budgets; • Oversee that accurate and complete financial records are maintained; • Review of the University financial statements and budgets and provide committee recommendations for Board approval; • Review of University’s debt • Facilitate the advancement of contemporary human resources systems, including progress in measuring and evaluation of community diversity and inclusion; • Facilitate the advancement of contemporary information technology systems. • Monitor campus facilitie s, grounds, maintenance, depreciation, deferred maintenance, and asset protection investments;

• Oversee contemporary, efficient, and timely procurement processes and investments, especially for the continuous improvement of the information technology infrastructure; and • Review that the long -range the campus master plan for facilities is updated periodically. University Liaisons: Vice President for Administration and Finance, Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs and Provost INDEX OF CHANGES 1. Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng.
President DATE: June 10, 2024 SUBJECT: Action Item: Approval of the University of Rhode Island FY2026-FY2030 Capital Improvement Plan Purpose of Submittal: The University is seeking approval from the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees for the submission of the University of Rhode Island FY2026-FY2030 Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) to the State of Rhode Island Department of Administration.
Recommendation: I recommend that the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees approve the enclosed University of Rhode Island FY2026-FY2030 Capital Improvement Plan (CIP).
Points to Consider: Every year, the University of Rhode Island submits a CIP to the State of Rhode Island.
The CIP shows capital projects of $1 million or more, in progress or proposed.

This plan is a critical and necessary step in securing funding to support the physical assets at the University and to assist with the advancement of educational and research programs that support the University’s faculty, staff, students, alumni, collaborative partners, and the citizens of the State.
The CIP identifies the projects, organizes them based on the priorities of the University, and associates a funding source with each.
The University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees has two opportunities to review the proposed CIP, first at the April Board meeting as an item for review and discussion, and next at the June Board meeting for final approval and submission to the State Office of Management and Budget (OMB).
The enclosed presentation provides updates to existing CIP projects scope/budget/schedule, including: • Narragansett Bay Campus Phase 1 and 2 • Fine Arts Center • Athletics Complex Renewal • Biomedical Sciences Building • New University Housing • Memorial Union • Health and Counseling Center

[Type here] The CIP also includes the following new projects added since last year’s submitted FY25-FY29 CIP, with a heavy emphasis on addressing the significant backlog of asset renewal needed on URI’s buildings, which in total comprise 28% of the State’s buildings. • Campus Accessibility • Building Envelope Improvements • Carothers HVAC Replacement • Campus Access Control • New Graduate Housing • Public Safety Building (new addition since Board consideration in April) • Automotive and Admin Services • NBC Shoreline Stabilization • New Water Tower Additionally, projects that have been removed (completed) are: • College of Engineering – Phase 2 (Bliss Hall) • Ryan Institute Lab – Phase 1 The FY2026-FY2030 CIP as recommended includes a total increase of approximately $580M. Supporting Information: Please see attached URI FY2026-FY2030 Capital Improvement Plan spreadsheet and supporting presentation. Proposed Motion of the Board: THAT, the Board of Trustees approve the University of Rhode Island Capital Improvement Plan for FY2026- FY2030 as presented.
CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PLAN FY26-FY30 Presentation to URI Board of Trustees Finance & Facilities Committee June 10, 2024

What is the Capital Improvement Plan? • 5 Year plan that shows projects that have a total project cost of greater than $1 Million • It is a rolling plan that is submitted annually as a request to the state, typically on July 1st. Who Approves the Capital Improvement Plan? • There are 5 levels of approval. They are: • University of Rhode Island - Facilities Committee (internal) (April & June) • University of Rhode Island - President ’s Executive Council (March & June) • University of Rhode Island - Board of Trustees (April & June) • Executive Branch • Analysis performed and Recommendations made by the Office of Management and Budget (July-December) • Final Approval by Governor’s Office (Third week of January) • Legislative Branch • Analysis performed and Recommendations made by both the House and Senate Fiscal Offices (January – June) • Final Plan approved as part of the RI Budget Appropriations Bill (June) How is a project added to the Capital Improvement Plan? • In order to receive consideration, all projects mu st be submitted on the Capital Improvement Request form by a member of the Senior Leadership to the URI Office of Planning & Real Estate Development • Most projects will have an advanced planning study performed prior to inclusion in the Capital Improvement plan to determine program, siting, massing, and total expected project cost
What does the Capital Improvement Plan cover? The University of Rhode Island’s Board of Trustees is responsible for about 28% of the State’s total real estate portfolio.
